draft.title: Waybill Preliminary Investment Case
draft.purpose: Assess value proposition, monetization clarity, and founder request alignment for early-stage hardware procurement automation.

sections.heading: Observed Customer Problem
sections.content: Hardware engineers spend weeks managing procurement: sourcing parts, chasing quotes, handling logistics, and tracking inventory. Manual processes lead to delays, errors, and inefficient capital use (E2, E5).

sections.heading: Value Creation
sections.content: Waybill automates end-to-end procurement: sourcing, negotiation, freight, customs, delivery, and inventory updates. Reduces time spent on procurement and improves supply chain visibility (E3, E5).

sections.heading: Monetization Model
sections.content: Pricing structure unspecified in evidence. Founder request for intros to procurement leads suggests B2B sales focus, but no explicit revenue model or pricing tiers are documented (E1, E3).

sections.heading: Founder Request Context
sections.content: Founder explicitly requests intros to procurement leads at hardware enterprises. This signals need for outreach assistance, not direct customer demand or willingness to pay (E1).

draft.title: Waybill Investment Case Assessment
draft.purpose: Evaluate procurement automation value proposition for hardware teams

sections.heading: Customer Problem
sections.content: Hardware engineers spend weeks on procurement: chasing quotes, managing approvals, tracking shipments, and reconciling inventory. Waybill automates sourcing, negotiation, freight, customs, delivery, and inventory tracking.

sections.heading: Value Creation
sections.content: End-to-end procurement automation reduces manual effort, accelerates time-to-shelf, and ensures inventory accuracy. Built on experience from LAT Aerospace and WareIQ (YC S20).

sections.heading: Monetization
sections.content: Unknown charging model. No explicit pricing or revenue metrics in evidence. Founder requests intros to procurement leads, not direct monetization claims.

sections.heading: Founder Request
sections.content: Request for introductions to procurement leads at hardware enterprises indicates need for outreach, not validated buyer demand or willingness to pay.

draft.decision_question: Does Waybill's automation create sufficient value to justify investment, given unknown monetization and early-stage traction?
draft.next_action: Prepare researched procurement-lead prospect brief and draft founder outreach proposal
draft.completion_test: Verify if proposed outreach leads to engagement with hardware procurement leads
